_comment: ⚠ 2026-08-23 (seventh) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 72 -> 74 for D196, THE BUFFERED SPECIAL. actor.attack_gesture_state gains buffered_special and nothing joins or leaves. ⭐ 73 IS SKIPPED, offered to the concurrent respawn-interval branch so two branches cannot both take one number — the same reasoning v53, v57 and v65 record. ⛔⛔ BodyActionBuffer::special was a bare TIMER while the attack slot beside it carried a whole AttackGestureIntent, and the buffer's own doc already said why that is wrong: 'a buffered press must be replayed verbatim rather than reinterpreted from the live stick later'. Replay called attack_dir_from_axis on the LIVE frame, so pressing Up+Special into a refusal and letting the stick centre produced a NEUTRAL special — and out of shield it did not even QUALIFY, because that rule asks whether the press RISES. ⭐ the intent carries a POSTURE as well as a direction, decided at the press rather than read off live ECS state at replay, so a kit with special_down and special_air_down gives the player the one they asked for. ⛔ AttackDir does NOT move into ambition_platformer2d_core: the generic timer is body-core state and the semantic intent is combat's, exactly as the attack slot is split today. ⚠ ResolvedAttackGesture gains a `special` field and costs NOTHING: it is declare_rollback_derived_component, republished every tick from the registered state above. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-23 (fifth) is THE AUTHORED ZERO, and it takes NO GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION bump — v72 stands. HitboxKnockback::LaunchSpeed::growth widens from f32 to Option<f32>, and Hitbox IS rollback state (entity:hitbox + combat.hitbox), so the instinct is to bump. ⛔ THE INSTINCT IS WRONG AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING: combat.hitbox is a component-CLONE row whose checksum projection is |hitbox| hitbox.owner. A clone row serializes nothing between peers and this one probes only the owner handle, so no byte any peer compares carries the growth at all. Nor can content make two builds disagree: every existing volume authored 0.0, the Strike builder maps its zero to None, and None resolves to base * ruleset_growth exactly as 0.0 did — while Some(0.0), the new value, cannot be written in a build that has not got the field. Same content, same launch, both sides. ⭐ this is the v38 shape: no payload moved behind an unchanged stable key. ⛔⛔ do not read this as 'clone rows never need a bump' — the day a projection reaches past `owner`, or a peer starts serializing this row, the growth joins the wire and the answer inverts. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-23 (fourth) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 71 -> 72 for the CEILING TECH. body.ground gains head_contact and nothing joins or leaves. ⭐ it is the OTHER END of the gravity axis on_ground already reports, sampled by the same pass and cleared beside it — and it is PERSISTED rather than read from the step's contacts because the floor game runs in the CONTROL phase, one phase before contacts exist. A ceiling tech has to be decidable at the top of the tick, exactly as the wall tech decides from BodyWallState::on_wall. ⛔ rewound with on_ground for the same reason it is: a restore without it decides a tech from the wrong tick's surface. ⚠ Contact::involuntary is NOT here and owes nothing: FrameEvents is per-step output, not rollback state. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-23 (third) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 70 -> 71 for the JAB CHAIN AND FLURRY (M5). actor.move_playback gains looped_s and nothing joins or leaves. ⭐ the lap count is state and the CLOCK is not enough: a loop rewinds `t` to where it already was, so only this says how long a flurry has been running — a rewind that restored the clock without it would resimulate with a fresh maximum and one peer's rapid jab would end while the other's did not. ⛔ MoveSpec::repeat is AUTHORED data and reaches a peer only through the move id the playback already encodes, like every other authored field. ⭐ the CHAIN adds no state at all: a follow-up press reads the cancel window's own `into` list forwards and starts the successor as an ordinary move, so a three-hit jab is three MoveSpecs and a cancel table rather than a mode. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-23 (second) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 69 -> 70 for the OUT-OF-SHIELD POLICY (M4). body.shield gains release_locked + drop_lag_timer, and the motion codec's AxisSweptParams gains ShieldTuning::drop_lag plus a one-byte out-of-shield table. Nothing joins or leaves. ⭐ the policy is Option: None is the engine baseline and means a raised guard restricts nothing and acting does not spend it, which is byte-identical to every body before this. Only ShieldTuning::PLATFORM_FIGHTER declares one, and only the smash demo uses that preset. ⭐ the table's bit 0 is PRESENCE, so a policy that permits nothing can never be confused with no policy at all. ⛔ release_locked is what makes an out-of-shield action a SPEND: without it a held button re-raises the guard on the next tick and re-arms the parry window with it, so acting out of shield would cost nothing and hand back a fresh perfect shield. ⛔ drop_lag_timer is its own clock and NOT stun_timer beside it: shieldstun is what a blocked hit charges and this is what letting go costs, and one timer for two causes is the mistake the ledge's borrowed dodge timer already taught this tree. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-23 bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 68 -> 69 for the LEDGE/DODGE SPLIT. AxisManeuverState gains ledge_invuln_timer and nothing joins or leaves — the model's private maneuver state is already on the wire whole (motion_codec), so this is one more f32 behind an unchanged stable key. ⭐ NOTHING CHANGES ABOUT WHAT REFUSES DAMAGE: the three ledge sites (the grab's earned window, the getup roll, the getup attack) moved off dodge_roll_timer onto their own, and BodyMotionFacts::evading gained ledge_intangible as a fourth term, so the same bodies are untouchable for the same spans. ⛔ the old field was shared on the argument that it 'already gates damage — same pipeline, single source of truth'. The pipeline was right and the FIELD was the wrong place to join it: the join belongs at evading(), which is what the damage rule reads, and sharing the timer made a body hanging on an edge indistinguishable from one mid-dodge-roll — a stale spot_dodging flag drew a ledge grab as a spot dodge, and neither window could be tuned without the other. ⚠ LEDGE_GETUP_ATTACK_INVULN is new and deliberately equal to the full attack: the getup attack's intangibility was INHERITED rather than decided, and this makes the decision visible without changing it. encoded_types and stable_schema_names are unchanged.

⚠ 2026-08-22 (fourth) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 66 -> 67 for MOVE INVULN AND SUPER ARMOR. actor.body_combat gains `armored` and nothing joins or leaves; Invulnerability gains a MOVE reason bit, which changes no encoding at all because the bitset was already carried whole. ⭐ WindowTag::Invuln and WindowTag::Armor were authoring vocabulary the runtime consumed NOWHERE — a move could declare either and the declaration changed nothing. They are answered by republishing onto facts the rest of combat already reads, never by teaching damage sites to inspect move timelines: intangibility becomes one more reason in the bitset body_vulnerable reads (so the `unhittable` presentation fact, which is that expression inverted, shows it with no presentation edit), and armor becomes BodyCombat::armored, which apply_body_hit_reaction already holds on both damage roads. ⭐ both are written EVERY tick for every combat body, move or not — a projection that only wrote while a move played would latch the last move's intangibility onto a body doing nothing. ⛔ `armored` is DERIVED and still encoded: the tick a rewind lands on reads it before the projection runs again, and a peer that decided a launch from a stale armor bit has already diverged. ⛔⛔ resolve_body_hit — the resolver BOTH damage roads share — now asks body_vulnerable instead of only combat.vulnerable(): the actor road, which every match fighter takes, asked nothing, so an evading or untouchable fighter was struck normally while the blink said otherwise. encoded_types stays 119 and stable_schema_names stays 365.

⚠ 2026-08-22 (third) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 64 -> 66 for the PARRY CATCH; 65 is skipped, offered to the concurrent presentation lane so two branches cannot both take one number (the same reasoning v53 and v57 record). body.shield gains parry_caught_timer and nothing joins or leaves. ⭐ it is a PRESENTATION window and still rollback state: a rewind that restored the guard without it would replay a parry with no beat, and two peers would draw different frames from one tick. ⛔⛔ the fact answers a question `parrying()` cannot — that one is the WINDOW being open, which is true of every raised guard for a few ticks, so a cue driven off it fires on every shield raise. ⭐ the parry is now RESOLVED at the one strike seam (apply_hitbox_damage) rather than at the two damage roads below it, which did not agree: the primary player's refused a parried hit inside body_vulnerable and the ACTOR road — the road every match fighter takes — never asked, so a fighter's parry was an ordinary block. A caught parry is a negation: no HitEvent, no LandedBodyHit, and no cost to the guard. encoded_types stays 119 and stable_schema_names stays 365; the three pre-existing codec-shape drifts named below are still not mine.

⚠ 2026-08-22 (second) bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 63 -> 64 for TRUE SMASH CHARGE, and again nothing joins or leaves. actor.move_playback gained a charge: the resolved hold policy, the proper-time hold accumulated so far, and the fraction FROZEN at release. ⭐ all three are hashed, not just the fraction: two peers whose held smash disagrees about elapsed hold land different damage and different knockback from the same move, and the policy rides along because it is resolved once at the move's start — a peer that rebuilt it from a differently-authored spec would agree about the elapsed hold and disagree about what it bought. ⛔ MoveSpec::smash_charge is AUTHORED data and not on the wire by itself; it reaches a peer only through the frozen copy on the playback. ⭐ the charge is per-USE, not per-move: only a press resolved as a Smash enters charge mode, so the same MoveSpec reached through another verb encodes None. encoded_types stays 119 and stable_schema_names stays 365; the three pre-existing codec-shape drifts named in the entry below are still not mine and still not re-recorded.

⚠ 2026-08-22 bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 62 -> 63 for the COMBAT ACTION INPUT BUFFER, and NOTHING JOINS OR LEAVES THIS FILE. Two already-registered rows changed what they ENCODE: body.action_buffer swapped its unfed `projectile` slot for `grab` + `special` (a ranged intent carries a direction, so a bare timer could never have replayed one — a reserved slot with a schema is not a feature), and actor.attack_gesture_state gained `buffered_press` while actor.attack_gesture_tuning gained `action_buffer_s`. ⭐ the clock and the intent are deliberately in TWO components: the window is body-generic and belongs on the body's own slot bag, the intent only exists because the gesture interpreter produced it, and re-resolving a buffered press from the live stick would silently downgrade every buffered smash to a tilt once its flick aged out. ⛔ ActorControl now #[require]s BodyActionBuffer, so every controlled body carries one — that widens the POPULATION under an unchanged registration, not the schema. ⚠ the codec-shape baseline was ALREADY STALE at this commit's parent for ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith, ambition_time and a pruned registry.rs row; those three are NOT re-recorded here, because laundering another change's drift into this one is how a ratchet stops meaning anything. encoded_types stays 119 and stable_schema_names stays 365.

⚠ 2026-08-20 ADDS TWO, and they are the FIRST body-vs-body contact in this format. GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 59 -> 60. `body.contact` is the capability itself — presence is the opt-in and the value is a RESISTANCE, so it is clone-registered and VALUE-PROBED rather than presence-only: two peers can agree a body is solid and disagree about how hard, which diverges every step that body takes beside another one. `derived.body_contact_snapshot` is the pre-integration sample the movement phase reads, DECLARED-DERIVED because it is cleared and refilled from authoritative BodyKinematics every tick with no already-applied gate. ⭐ encoded_types is UNCHANGED: a component-clone registration and a derived declaration write no SnapshotState impl, so no type joined the byte format. ⛔ the snapshot is a separate system from the integrator on purpose — a body that asked the world for its neighbours' LIVE poses would see whoever moved first already integrated, and query order would decide who won the contest, which is a desync.

⚠ 2026-08-19 FINISHES the slot-owned control migration with NO GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION bump. It PRUNES derived.player_input_frame: the per-body frame was only a declared-derived copy of derived.slot_controls and encoded no snapshot payload. Brain::Player(slot) now reads the slot-owned frame directly and body mechanics consume ActorControl. Set membership changes already move the schema fingerprint; v38 remains correct because no payload changed behind an unchanged stable key. encoded_types stays at 83.

⚠ v38 (2026-08-18) FINISHES the projectile spawn-road migration. It PRUNES resource.enemy_projectile_state, projectile.player_marker, projectile.enemy_marker, and projectile.owner_id. EnemyProjectileState was a field-less legacy pool handle; the two marker rows only remembered which historical spawn road selected presentation; the string owner id duplicated ProjectileOwner(Entity) and had no production reader. Every live shot is now one LiveProjectile occurrence, ownership is ProjectileOwner, presentation is optional ProjectileKind plus ProjectileVisualId, and combat side is the independently frozen ProjectileAllegiance. message.spawn_projectile keeps the SAME stable key but its concrete message becomes ProjectileSpawnRequest. GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 37 -> 38 because the registered state set changed deliberately.

⚠ 2026-08-17 ADDS message.run_authored_command and bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 35 -> 36 (D127 M1, the COMMAND half of the authored-logic contract). One channel carries every authored verb: a .yarn `<<command "domain.verb" arg…>>` line, or any sim system, asks for a command the owning domain published, and one drained dispatcher in AuthoredCommandSet performs it. ⭐ the buffer is normally EMPTY at a save boundary — the dispatcher drains inside the frame the narrative ledger released into and holds no MessageReader cursor — so this covers the one window that is not: a request released onto a frame the host rewinds past before the set ran, which the ledger re-releases and which would otherwise fire twice. ⛔ CommandCatalog itself is NOT here and must not be: `publish` is private, the only way in is PublishCommand on App, and a tick holds a World — the same structural argument that waives ConditionCatalog. ⚠ stable_schema_name_count read 357 against a 358-entry list before this commit; the field was stale, and 359 is the corrected count.

⚠ 2026-08-16 RENAMES resource.inventory_restored to resource.save_restored and bumps GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION 33 -> 34. No value and no projection moved — it is still a bare clone with no checksum, for the reason its own registration records (the systems run in literal Update, outside resimulation, so projecting the bool desynced the checksum). What changed is what the latch MEANS: it stopped answering 'has the catalog been applied?' and started answering 'has the loaded save been applied?', because the DURABLE occurrence horizon (ambition_platformer2d_actor_monolith::session::durable_horizon) reads it too. ⭐ deliberately ONE latch: two would be two answers to a single question, free to disagree the first time one leg's precondition was met and the other's was not. ⚠ the bump is for the row KEY, which is part of the wire identity — two peers whose schemas differ here cannot agree about a snapshot even though no byte of the value moved. ⛔ NOTHING was added for the durable save itself, and that is the finding worth keeping: the save file is not rollback state. The three values it serializes (resource.occurrence_baseline, resource.custody_baseline, resource.minted_item_baseline) were already registered as of v32/v33, and a durable LOAD writes them through the same adopt-and-resume road a death takes.

⚠ 2026-08-15 ADDS derived.placement_continuity, the FIRST durable-room-state row and a DECLARED-DERIVED one. AuthoredOccurrences answers the question a rebuilt room cannot ask its own authored records: what became of the occurrence this record minted last time? Its only producing leg (persisting) is republished WHOLE every tick from the live InCustodyOf population, which is itself derived from the registered item.item_custody, so it carries no already-applied gate, converges on the step after a rewind, and GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION stays at 31 - no encoding changed. It exists because custody let an authored object cross a room boundary alive, and re-entering the room then minted a SECOND occurrence claiming the same SimId::placement(..). ⛔⛔ the day OccurrenceDisposition::Consumed gains a producer this row becomes a lie: that leg ACCUMULATES a fact no live component still carries, nothing re-derives it, and it will owe a real registration with a value projection over the id set plus a durable-save representation, in the same change.

⚠ 2026-08-15 ADDS derived.custody_residency, a DECLARED-DERIVED row rather than a registration: InCustodyOf is recomputed unconditionally every tick from the registered item.item_custody, with no 'already applied' gate, so it is not rollback state and GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION stays at 31 — no encoding changed. It exists so a held item's RESIDENCY follows its holder: the roster a room change retires is now (With<RoomScopedEntity>, Without<InCustodyOf>), which is how a carried object crosses a room boundary without the transition knowing that items exist. ⛔ deliberately NOT _component_state: its only value is an entity handle, and hashing a raw handle is the hazard item.item_custody's entity-set probe already answers through the holder's SimId.

⚠ v31 (2026-08-15) ADDS resource.gate_portal_phases, and the growth is deliberate: the portal phase was a mutable f32 timer that nothing rewound. The switch driving it lives in AmbitionGameSave and IS registered, so the INPUT rewound while its INTEGRAL did not, leaving the phase permanently ahead by the depth of every rollback taken during the ~38-tick opening window. Its consumer refuses a room crossing unless the phase is On, so peers disagreed about whether the crossing happened. It was previously waived as 'authored' — a true sentence about GatePortalConfig, which really is authored, and which no longer holds the phase at all. Registered with a VALUE projection, not a presence probe: a presence probe would have restored that phases exist, said nothing about elapsed, and passed while reproducing the defect.

⚠ v28 (2026-08-14) REMOVES resource.combat_slot_board, and a removal is the rarer direction for this file. The board it rewound arranged a crowd into numbered approach slots around a target; no production reader consumed the assignment, so peers agreed every tick about a value nothing asked for. Its anchor was PrimaryPlayer-or-lowest-PlayerSlot, which made it the largest player-centric assumption inside generic actor simulation as well. Deleted with the board rather than made target-relative: target-relative arbitration for a mechanism with no consumer is the abstraction, not the fix.
The rollback wire format, frozen. Two keys, one invariant each way: a type
may not join it unseen, and a type that leaves must be PRUNED here in the
same commit. That second half is what makes this a ratchet and not a budget.
⚠ RENAMED `central_codecs` -> `encoded_types` on 2026-07-30 (slice F). The
old key named a FILE — `ambition_platformer2d_runtime/src/rollback/codecs.rs` — because
the orphan rule forced ~100 foreign impls into it: the trait sat above every
crate whose types it encoded. Slice F moved the trait to the floor
(`ambition_platformer2d_core::snapshot`) and the impls home to their own crates.
⚠ The rename found a blind spot rather than causing one. All 62 previously
frozen types are still present; the count went to 63 because `MotionModel`
was encoded in `motion_codec.rs`, a SECOND file the single-file collector
never read. A guard that says 'the wire format' while reading one of two
files is the failure this repo keeps rediscovering — it was green, and it
was green about less than it claimed.

⚠ S4 (2026-07-30) added five entries, and they are a JOIN rather than a drift: FighterStocks and FighterEliminated are the stocks loop's own state — a stock count that is not rollback state UN-SPENDS itself on a rewind, so a fighter loses the same stock twice or never loses it at all — plus message.body_knocked_out and message.fighter_stock_spent, which must be CLEARED on load or a rewound KO is re-read and spends a second stock. derived.resolved_combat_tuning is AE6's projection, declared derived rather than registered as state on purpose: restoring it independently of the declaration that produced it is the borrow the seam removed.

⚠ S4's match-end half (2026-07-31) joins two more: StocksMatchSettled is the 'already announced' latch, registered as STATE rather than left a Local because a rewind across the deciding frame must be able to UN-decide the match — a latch that survived it would swallow the re-announcement on the replay and the ruleset would never hear the match end. message.stocks_match_decided is cleared on load for the same reason.
⚠ SR-0 (2026-08-04) adds rollback encodings for accumulated proper time and the derived 2D relativity sample; TwinTrack is the concrete acceptance game.

⚠ SR-1 (2026-08-05) adds canonical coordinate time, proper-time cooldown, emitter, receiver/pool configuration, analytic light-signal, and bounded arrival-history encodings. The joins are deliberate: course rules depend on emission identity, passbands, deterministic slot allocation, cooldown state, and event history surviving rewind.
⚠ SR-2 (2026-08-05) adds canonical optical-source and observer declarations while keeping the optical view and worldline reconstruction derived.

⚠ SR-3 (2026-08-05) adds the canonical RelativisticTarget2d declaration used by exact constant-velocity null-intercept targeting. TwinTrack aim, view mode, pursuit timing, and hit results are carried inside its existing canonical experiment component and require rollback schema v10.

⚠ Cutscene playback joins the wire format (2026-08-06). ActiveCutscene::is_playing() drives a CAPTURING input-context claim, so whether the participant can act is gameplay truth rather than the "scripted presentation sequence state" the rollback_coverage waiver calls it — a rewind into a playing frame that did not restore it would let the resimulation act through beats the original could not. The codec encodes the SEMANTIC half only (script, beat index, elapsed, finished); dialogue line, banner, camera target and fade alpha are derived and re-published by the tick. ✔ REGISTERED 2026-08-06 as `cutscene.playback`, OPTIONAL-canonical because a composition without cutscenes carries no ActiveCutscene and the plain form's checksum system panics on a missing resource. Schema v10 -> v11: a v10 peer cannot reconstruct whether the participant was allowed to act.

⚠ SCHEMA v16 (2026-08-08) added six entries, and every one of them is a JOIN: the narrative boundary. actor.pending_challenge + map.pending_challenge are an ARMED challenge counting down to a fight — a sim system removes it, so a rewind past that removal kept the removal and disarmed the fight. message.conversation_ended, message.challenge_requested, message.item_grant_requested and message.shop_transaction_requested are what the non-rewound Yarn runner tells the simulation, released from the conversation ledger on the tick they were stamped for and cleared on load so a resimulated tick is HANDED them rather than remembering them. Three of the four had no message at all before: <<give_item>>, <<buy_item>> and <<challenge>> reached into rollback state from Update.

⚠ SCHEMA v17 (2026-08-08) adds actor.active_combatant, and it is a JOIN with a lifecycle the markers beside it do not have: RulesetOwnsDeath is attached at seating and never removed, while this one is REMOVED on elimination. A rewind past an elimination has to put it back, or the replayed branch runs with a fighter that is out of a match it has not lost yet. It replaces TWO proxies — RulesetOwnsDeath in CombatStanding::of and Has<MatchSeat> in the stand-down guard — neither of which meant 'is this body in a fight'.

⚠ v18 (2026-08-08) is the TwinTrack Relativity Plaza/Festival overlay, merged rather than unpacked: it was cut 2026-08-06 from a branch predating a301a79a0, so main's newer relativity API won where the two disagreed. ⚠ NOTHING CHANGES IN THIS FILE FOR IT, and that is the point worth writing down: this ratchet reads the RUNTIME's registrations (rollback/registry.rs + rollback/domains/**), and every `twintrack.*` name is registered by the demo crate, which the scanner never reads. The live dump in game/ambition_app/tests/rollback_schema_baseline.txt is the one that moves — it recorded twintrack.chase_beacon leaving and twintrack.character joining. Adding a demo-side name here reports STALE immediately, because the scanner cannot see it.

⚠ v19 (2026-08-08) is D29, and NOTHING CHANGES IN THIS FILE FOR IT — recorded because a version bump with no set movement is the case somebody will otherwise go looking for a missing entry. `ConversationInstanceId` took the `DialogueContext` INTO itself (`$speaker_id`/`$listener_id`, which content branches on, and which resolve from the initiator's rollback-owned `WornCharacter`), so two corrected timelines that differ in who is speaking stop sharing an identity. No name joins or leaves: the same `resource.active_conversation` registration now hashes a richer id and no longer hashes the context beside it. This ratchet freezes WHICH types are on the wire; the version constant is the only signal for a change to what one of them ENCODES.

⚠ message.conversation_cut_bark (2026-08-08) is the continuity → CAST port: the break rule asks for a bark, the cast answers on the same tick. It exists so `conversation` stops naming crate::features and crate::character_runtime — its last two inward edges — which is what makes the module liftable. Cleared on load like every other in-tick sim channel: a request from a branch the host abandoned must not reach the cast. ⚠ NO version bump: a message-clear row adds no bytes to a snapshot, so two peers differing only in this still agree about every value.

⚠ v20 (2026-08-09) is D37, and NOTHING CHANGES IN THIS FILE FOR IT — recorded for the same reason v19 was: a version bump with no set movement is the case somebody will otherwise go looking for a missing entry. `schema_dump()` stopped writing a type's crate and module path and now writes its FINAL SEGMENT alone, so relocating a rollback-registered type is no longer a wire-format change — which is what stops every carve in the decomposition campaign from being a netplay compatibility break. It is the second half of the decision v5 made about `owner`: an organisational label is not a wire-format fact, and nobody chose this one, it arrived inside a string being used for identity. No stable name joins or leaves and no projection changed; only the hashed spelling of each type moved, and the version constant is the only signal for that. ⚠ the narrower identity is sound only while final segments are unique, so `try_register` now REJECTS two DIFFERENT types that share one — two crates each spelling a `Cooldown` is the shape it names, and `encoded_types` below is where to look when it fires.

⚠ SCHEMA v21 (2026-08-09) is ADR 0033, and it adds two entries that are a JOIN: actor.out_of_play and actor.death_interlude. Death stopped being an event the world resolves in the frame it happens and became a STATE the ruleset resolves, so 'this participant's attempt is over', 'its window has N seconds left' and 'it still owes the game its consequence' are gameplay truth that must survive a rewind. The debt field is the one that had to be learned twice: the level reset it triggers is a message written in one frame and consumed in the next, so a rewind across that boundary loses the request unless the cause is answerable from state — measured as a sync-test checksum mismatch on a route that was green. ⚠ they REPLACE a game-side registration: Mary-O's content.mary_o_death_sequence carried the same facts for one game and was clone-probed rather than checksummed, so the wire format gained the truth it was already relying on rather than gaining a feature.

⚠ SCHEMA v22 (2026-08-09) makes the resolved body hit the on-hit seam. feature.pogo_target and map.hitbox_on_hit are PRUNED because ordinary combat bodies no longer become anonymous world pogo blocks and HitboxOnHit no longer owns a per-victim entity set; message.landed_body_hit joins as a load-cleared same-frame channel. HitboxOnHit itself also changed encoded fields from EffectRef + victim set to EffectRef + world_fired, so the version bump is required even beyond the descriptor-set movement: a v21 peer would decode different bytes.

⚠ 2026-08-16 ADDS FIVE, and they are the RESET HORIZON — the first values in this format that nothing republishes. GGRS_ROLLBACK_SCHEMA_VERSION went 31 -> 32 in the same landing. message.checkpoint_committed and message.reset_to_checkpoint are the two channels of the horizon (a shrine rest; a death), both registered with clear_message_on_rollback because a message that survives a rewind fires its consumer twice. resource.occurrence_baseline and resource.custody_baseline are the checkpoint's SNAPSHOT of two authoritative domains — ⭐ deliberately two, not one: an AuthoredOccurrences row says SOMEBODY holds the occurrence and cannot say WHICH body, so custody keeps its own projection and the baseline is a projection of domains rather than a clone of one resource.
